content_units: 90-Minute Talent Showcase Plan

For a school arts club showcase on   Saturday, 14 November 2026  , this running order keeps energy high, avoids long reset gaps, and fits the   18:30-20:00   slot with   10 acts max  . It uses alternating pace: big start, variety in the middle, and a memorable finale.
Running Order and Stage Flow
Slot   Time   Act   Length   Transition Plan
1   18:30-18:36   Opening Group Percussion or Dance   6 min   Starts immediately as audience settles; no intro beyond quick welcome
2   18:36-18:42   Emcee Welcome + Solo Singer   6 min   Singer uses center mic already preset
3   18:42-18:50   Comedy Monologue or Spoken Word Duo   8 min   Clears stage fast; no equipment reset
4   18:50-18:58   Small Band / Acoustic Ensemble   8 min   Set up during prior act if possible at stage side
5   18:58-19:05   Short Drama Scene or Sketch   7 min   Minimal props only; strike handled by cast on exit
6   19:05-19:12   Instrumental Solo or Duet   7 min   Emcee fills while chair/stand is placed
7   19:12-19:20   Dance Feature   8 min   Strong visual lift after seated act
8   19:20-19:27   Magic, Variety, or Novelty Act   7 min   Keeps second half unpredictable
9   19:27-19:37   Choir, Vocal Group, or Collaborative Medley   10 min   Big ensemble feel builds toward close
10   19:37-19:50   Finale: Full-Cast Mash-up / Signature Showcase Act   13 min   Strong closing image; all performers join curtain call setup
This leaves about   10 minutes total buffer   for applause, short resets, late starts, and a closing thank-you.
Recommended Act Mix
Use this balance to keep the program varied and efficient:
Option 1:   Opening Percussion/Dance     High-energy start that grabs attention instantly   Best opener
Stage cue sheet
Option 2:   Singer or Vocal Solo     Emotional contrast after the opener   Fast setup
Mic checklist
Option 3:   Comedy or Spoken Word     Zero-complexity reset slot; ideal between equipment-heavy acts   Dead-time reducer
Script notes
Option 4:   Finale Group Medley     Best closer because it feels celebratory and includes more students   Strong ending
Rehearsal plan
Emcee Script You Can Use
Opening at 18:30

“Good evening everyone, and welcome to the School Arts Club Talent Showcase. We’re so glad you’re here with us tonight. Our performers have worked hard to put together a fun, creative programme full of music, movement, drama, and surprises. Please give every act your full support, and if you enjoy what you see, let them hear it. Let’s begin with a performance guaranteed to start the night with energy.”
Between acts
“Let’s hear it once again for that performance.”
“Coming up next, we’re shifting gears with something completely different.”
“While the stage is being reset, here’s a quick reminder to keep cheering loudly for your classmates.”
“Our next act brings a different style and mood, which is exactly what tonight is all about.”
Before the finale
“We’ve reached the final performance of the evening, and it’s a special one. Please give a huge welcome to our closing act.”
Closing at 19:50-20:00

“What a fantastic evening of talent. Thank you to all our performers, student crew, teachers, and families for making tonight possible. Please give one more round of applause for everyone who took part. Have a safe trip home, and thank you for supporting the arts.”
Transition Design That Cuts Dead Time
- Put   low-tech acts   right after any performance needing equipment changes.
- Use   side-stage setup  : next act waits ready with props/instruments before prior act ends.
- Keep all props to   one-trip items  ; avoid furniture-heavy scenes.
- Mark the stage with   tape positions   for mic stands, chairs, and center spots.
- Have   2 student stage crew   assigned only to moving stands/chairs.
- Preload backing tracks in   one playlist  , in exact show order, with volume checked.
- Use one   wireless handheld mic   and one   center stand mic   as the default setup.
- Tell performers:   enter fast, bow fast, exit fast  .
A practical pacing rule:
-   Big act
-   Simple act
-   Tech act
-   Simple act
This pattern prevents back-to-back reset delays.
If an Act Ends 5 Minutes Early
Keep 3-4 backup fillers prepared so the audience feels the change is intentional.
-   Audience clap challenge  : emcee divides room into left/right sections for loudest applause.
-   Performer mini-interview  : 2 quick questions to the previous act backstage or on stage edge.
-   Spotlight shout-outs  : thank crew, music operator, art club leaders, and teachers.
-   Audience vote by applause  : funniest, most surprising, most energetic act so far.
-   Pop-up encore fragment  : ask a singer or instrumentalist to repeat a 60-90 second section.
-   Club promo moment  : invite students to join the arts club or next production.
Best emergency filler sequence for 5 minutes:
1. 45-second applause reset
2. 90-second emcee audience interaction
3. 90-second performer Q&A
4. 60-second sponsor/thank-you note
5. 30-second intro into next act
Audience Energy Plan
- Start with your   most visual   act.
- Put a   comedy/spoken word   piece around the first third to refresh attention.
- Avoid stacking more than   2 slower acts   in a row.
- Use the emcee to frame each change in mood so the program feels deliberate.
- Encourage applause cues: “Give them a big welcome” and “One more time for…”
- Keep house lights slightly up during transitions so the room feels alive, not stalled.
Practical Setup Notes for a Dublin School Hall
Given a typical school hall setup, this plan assumes:
- a   single main stage area
- basic   PA system with 2 mics
- phone/laptop playback for tracks
- simple lighting with general wash, not theatrical scene changes
If available, add:
- one   stage manager
- one   sound operator
- one   backstage lineup sheet   with all performers called   2 acts ahead
